title: Methods
bodyHtml:
Meta-analyses

We assembled results from three large biobanks with sequencing data (see Figure). We performed gene-based testing of three masks using mixed-effects models, and performed a meta-analysis across the datasets. The masks included 1) a mask with rare LOF variants (MAF<0.1%), 2) a mask with rare LOF and highly predicted-deleterious missense variants (missense score >=0.8), and 3) a mask with ultra-rare missense variants that were predicted deleterious (missense score >=0.5; MAF<0.001%), as shown in the Figure. The variants in each mask were also restricted to gnomAD popmax<0.1%. The stringent frequency cutoffs were chosen to limit results to very rare genetic variation in an attempt to enforce orthogonality to conventional common variant GWAS results.

Prior to meta-analysis, we removed gene-based results with cMAC<20 in a dataset. After meta-analysis, we combined the P-values from each mask into a single P-value using the Cauchy distribution test (see Figure). Please consult the associated manuscript for details on the missense score and in-depth methodology.

Effect sizes

Effect sizes for phecode-mask pairs can be found using the gene search. For all associations, effect sizes are on the log(Odds Ratio) scale. For all gene-based associations reaching P<1x10-5, we re-estimated mask effect sizes using Firth’s bias-reduced logistic regression. Therefore, effect sizes on the portal are highly accurate for genes with significant results.
